notes.title: Colossal Cave VR 2.0: The Enchanted Edition
notes.content:
From the Desk of Roberta Williams …

I am very proud to announce our updated Colossal Cave 2.0, our new ‘enchanted cave’ version! I have always admired this historic text adventure, referring to it as deeply engaging and captivating -- and arguably the spark that ignited the onset of computer gaming – and have desired for many years to bring it to life with beautiful graphics, atmospheric sounds, and characters of charm…or roguery. This has always been an enchanted cave which – beware! -- is also your adversary, and it was important that we capture that imagery and spirit. I am now so excited by our considerable efforts that I urge everyone to check out our latest release, Colossal Cave 2.0. My team and I have been hard at work the last eight months since our January release of Colossal Cave perfecting playability while also enhancing the mysterious, metaphysical, and immersive nature of Colossal Cave.

Be sure to check out our recent [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aXUddxm8WoU]360-degree trailer on YouTube[/url].  Best viewed in a headset, set to 360-degrees!: 

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aXUddxm8WoU][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44201598/2fca378771faaf287c352794e2388e599ca50a92.gif[/img][/url]

Ahead of this undertaking, I reviewed the many reactions to our initial release – both positive and negative. I adapted or corrected the unfavorable responses while at the same time maintaining or improving the complimentary ones – though always keeping in mind the essence of the original gameplay which, to me, is sacrosanct. As a game designer myself, I recognize a great design. It is my humble opinion that the original Colossal Cave has stood the test of time due to the innovative and imaginative minds of Will Crowther and Don Woods, the original creators of this classic text adventure game. When Ken and I decided to reimagine Colossal Cave, I swore not to change the gameplay and strategy of these two ingenious men. Although, to be fair, there are those who would argue that by adding 3D graphics, character animations, sound effects, or music – and even a point-and-click interface – that would be changing it. Well, yes – I do agree with that. But still, my assertion is that, as with any script of a story, or a design strategy of a game, the means of experiencing it can be done in various ways or means, similar to reading a book and then experiencing that same story in a movie.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43213921/38467c7279edb87bf1ee48a4e6e0ed1bfe87ca21.gif[/img]

I am very excited for players of all ages – but for those who especially love adventure games – to experience Colossal Cave 2.0. Broadly speaking, here are the enrichments:

[list]
[*] Enhanced graphics (higher-resolution textures, post-processing to enhance colors, more real-time lighting and shadows, realistic-looking water, magical effects, particle effects with mist, fog, and smoke – among other graphical embellishments).
[*] The addition of player footstep sound effects while traversing the Colossal Cave world. And I took great care to make them sound very realistic.
[*] More atmospheric sound effects really bring the cave alive. I imagined the cave having a spirit, an essential ‘being’ without a body. There is an ‘aliveness,’ but also mystery and magic.
[*] Improving the animation of the many characters inhabiting the cave – giving them more charm…or nastiness!
[*] The cave itself is your adversary – not any one of the characters. It really is between YOU and the CAVE.
[*] Bettering the IU, the interface. To make Colossal Cave – 2.0 easy to play without having to figure out the interface. Playing the game is enough to think about!
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44201598/c1af1917cb86c56816a7b10f9aa69d92207b701d.gif[/img]

All my best,

Roberta
